rulers.name: Theodoric the Great
rulers.note: Entered Ravenna 5 March 493 (reign from 15 March 493 in the infobox); died 30 August 526. Clipped to the dossier's start (500) by the reviewer (eu-06-e); 493-499 is the ostrogoths dossier.

rulers.name: Athalaric
rulers.note: Succeeded Theodoric under Amalasuntha as regent; died 2 October 534.

rulers.name: Amalasuntha
rulers.title: regent for Athalaric
rulers.note: Crowned Theodahad in 534; executed in early May 535.

rulers.name: Theodahad
rulers.note: Crowned by Amalasuntha in 534; died before Vitiges was proclaimed in late 536.

rulers.name: Vitiges
rulers.note: Proclaimed late 536 near Regata; surrendered Ravenna in May 540.

rulers.name: Ildibad
rulers.note: Reign 'c. Late summer 540 - May 541' (infobox); elected king in 540 and 'moved his capital to Pavia'; murdered at a royal banquet in May 541.

rulers.name: Eraric
rulers.note: Killed in October 541 (Ildibad page); the page gives no date for his accession, taken here as 541.

rulers.name: Totila
rulers.note: Proclaimed in autumn 541; killed at Taginae in 552.

rulers.name: Teia
rulers.note: Defeated with the last Gothic army at Mons Lactarius, October 553; 'His death marks the end of the Ostrogothic Kingdom' (Ostrogothic Kingdom page).

correction.text: Theodoric's Italy, Sicily, the Alpine provinces and Dalmatia, without Sirmium (held by the Gepids until 504)

keyframe_review.note: 556,166 km2 for 500-509, Italy, Sicily, the Alps and Pannonia, 6.6-20.3 E, 36.7-49.2 N; Cliopatria's Ostrogoths row (490-499) is the same realm and its Italian part is 1.07 times this shape's (eu-06-d). The shape holds the Sirmium district from 500, but the Gepids page has the Gepids in Sirmium from 473 until Pitzia expelled them in 504; the shape also lacks the Dalmatian coast (Salona is outside it in every year). The correction for 500-503 takes Sirmium out and puts Dalmatia in (the Ostrogoths dossier, eu-06-d, hands Dalmatia over in 493; the Gothic War page has it Gothic in 535). No page opened gives an area (the Ostrogothic Kingdom page's infobox has none), so the factor-of-two check is not possible. The Alpine cells (Raetia, the south of Alamannia) stay: the Alemanni 'put themselves under the protection of Theodoric', which the ledger records as a vassal tint.

correction.text: Theodoric's Italy, Sicily, the Alpine provinces, Dalmatia and Pannonia round Sirmium

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 504-509: Sirmium joins. 'In 504-505, Theodoric's forces launched a campaign to recover Pannonia and the strategically important town of Sirmium' (Ostrogothic Kingdom page); the Gepids page: 'Comes Pitzia expelled the Gepid troops from Sirmium without much resistance' in 504. correction.text: Italy, Sicily, the Alps, Dalmatia, Pannonia round Sirmium and Provence from 510

keyframe_review.note: 574,011 km2 for 510-533: the 500 shape plus 94 cells of Provence (4.1-8.9 E, 43-44 N), less 17 cells east of Sirmium. 'starting in 508, Theodoric's generals campaigned in Gaul' and 'extending Ostrogothic rule into southern Gaul'; 'There in 510 Theodoric reestablished the defunct praetorian prefecture of Gaul.' The Provence addition is right in year and place. Two corrections: the shape puts Sirmium's own cell in the Gepid shape (the Gepids lost Sirmium in 504 and regained it only in 536), and it still lacks Dalmatia. The 511 control over the Visigothic kingdom (Theodoric page) is a vassal tint, not drawn here.

correction.text: the Ostrogothic Kingdom at its greatest, Theodoric's realm under Theodahad, with Sirmium and Dalmatia

keyframe_review.note: 576,943 km2 for 534-535, 2,900 km2 more than the 510 shape with nothing in the pages to explain it (the Ostrogothic Kingdom page has Athalaric die on 2 October 534 and Amalasuntha crown Theodahad). Kept; Sirmium and Dalmatia added as in 510-533.

452,700 km2 for 536-539: Sicily (Belisarius landed in December 535), Dalmatia (Mundus took Salona in March 536 and by late June 'the whole of Dalmatia was in Byzantine hands'), Naples (November 536) and the Alpine cells are gone, and Provence stays to 539. The shape fits the Gothic War page except that Rome is drawn Gothic although Belisarius entered it unopposed in December 536 (the Goths only besieged it, March 537 to March 538), and that the Sirmium cell is already the Gepids'. Provence goes to the Franks only in the 540 shape.

correction.text: the Gothic remainder after the fall of Ravenna: Ticinum (Pavia), Verona and Brescia in the north of the Po, with the Cliopatria Pannonian shape

keyframe_review.note: 206,265 km2 for 540-545, Pannonia and the Dalmatian hinterland (8.4-19.9 E, 43.3-48.3 N) with none of Italy: Ravenna, Milan and Verona are all outside it. The Gothic War page: 'In May 540, Belisarius and his army entered Ravenna. ... The Goths held Ticinum (Pavia), Verona, and parts of the north of the Po.' The correction keeps the Cliopatria Pannonian remainder (unverified: no page opened has Goths in Pannonia after 536; the Alboin page has the Lombards moving in 'while the Ostrogothic Kingdom was weakened') and adds Verona, Brescia and Pavia, the strongholds the Gothic War page names to 562. Holds for 540 only; 541-542 and 543-545 are the next two keyframes.

correction.text: the Goths of the north: Pavia, Verona, Brescia, Venetia and Liguria, with the Cliopatria Pannonian shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 541-542: 'Gothic control was re-established over Venetia and Liguria under Ildibad' (Gothic War page, 'Goth holdings, 541-546'); Totila was proclaimed king in the autumn of 541. Venetia is drawn as the Veneto and Liguria as Liguria.

correction.text: the north (Pavia, Verona, Brescia, Venetia, Liguria) and Totila's reconquest of the south from 543, with the Cliopatria Pannonian shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 543-545: 'Totila ... retook much of southern Italy, including Naples in 543'; 'Totila held the south, Tuscany, and Rome' (Rome only from 17 December 546). The south is drawn as Cliopatria's 546 shape, which holds Naples and Campania and 152 cells south of Rome that the 545 shape lacked.

correction.text: Totila's Italy with the strongholds of the Gothic north (Pavia, Verona, Brixia) and the share of Venetia that Cliopatria's 546 shape holds

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 546 shape: 77,803 km2 (8.4-18.4 E, 39.9-47.1 N), Italy north of Rome plus the south, Pannonia gone. Rome fell to Totila on 17 December 546, Belisarius retook it in the spring of 547, Totila took it again in 549-550, and after Taginae (552) 'Rome then capitulated'. The Gothic War page keeps the north in Gothic hands (Pavia 'became the new capital of the Ostrogothic Kingdom', Verona and Brixia held to 562), but the shape holds none of Pavia's 15 cells and 4 of Verona's 12, so the capital (Pavia 540-553, infobox) lay outside the state. Review fix 2026-10-20: Pavia, Verona and Brescia are added (326 cells, about 82,000 km2). Venetia and Liguria are not added wholesale, against the reviewer's suggestion: the Theudebert I page says that 'During the Ostrogothic resurgence under King Totila, Theudebert seized the opportunity' and 'captured the Cottian Alps, parts of the Liguria region, and the greater part of Venetia' (he died at the end of 547 or the start of 548), and Cliopatria's 546 shape holds 34 of the Veneto's 71 cells and none of Liguria's 24; the loss is a ledger event at 546. The years change: the keyframe ends in 551 and the next gives the north alone from 552. The Rome interlude of 547-549 is in the ledger.

correction.text: the Gothic north after Taginae and Mons Lactarius: Cliopatria's 555 rump with Pavia (the capital to 553), Verona and Brescia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 552-554: the peninsula is lost with Totila's death at Taginae and the last army at Mons Lactarius ('In October 553' on the Gothic War page; October 552 on the Teia page); the Goths keep the north, 'The lands and cities across the River Po were still held by Franks, Alemanni, and Goths' (Gothic War page). Cliopatria's 555 rump (32,729 km2, 8.4-14.0 E, 45.5-46.7 N) holds none of Pavia and 4 of Verona's 12 cells; Review fix 2026-10-20: Pavia (Teia 'withdrew to Ticinum ... the capital of the Gothic Kingdom'; infobox capital to 553), Verona and Brescia are added (162 cells, about 41,000 km2). Pavia's fall is dated nowhere on the pages (Gothic War, Ostrogothic Kingdom, Teia): it is held here to 554 and lost at 555, Cliopatria's rump year, at confidence 1. Campsa near Naples, where seven thousand Goths held out until the spring of 555, is not drawn.

Cliopatria's 555 shape: 32,729 km2 for 555-560, the north (8.4-14.0 E, 45.5-46.7 N). 'The last Gothic and Frankish strongholds, Verona and Brescia (Brixia), were subjugated in 562' (Gothic War page), but the shape holds 4 of Verona's 12 cells and 11 of Brescia's 18. Review fix 2026-10-20: the whole of Verona and Brescia are added (147 cells, about 37,000 km2); Pavia, the capital to 553, is lost at 555 (ledger, confidence 1). The years are extended by the next keyframe.

region.text: Theodoric's Italy, Sicily, the Alpine provinces and Dalmatia

ledger.note: 500: the Cliopatria row of the Ostrogothic Kingdom begins. The kingdom itself dates from 493: 'Theodoric entered Ravenna on 5 March 493' (Theodoric the Great page), and the Ostrogoths dossier (eu-06-d) holds Italy 493-499 and hands it over here; the year is the Cliopatria seam, confidence 1. The Theodoric page has him recognised by the emperor ('Anastasius in 497' per the Ostrogothic Kingdom page).

region.text: the southern Alamannian lands round Lake Constance, under Theodoric's protection

ledger.note: From 496 the southern half of the Alemannic lands is under Theodoric's protection. After 496 the Alemanni 'put themselves under the protection of Theodoric the Great of the Ostrogoths' (Alemanni page); the Tolbiac page: 'the southern half sought protection under Theoderic'. Placed at 500 because this dossier starts there (confidence 1); the Ostrogoths dossier covers 496-499 and does not record it. The Alamannia page's infobox is reported to read 'Ostrogothic Kingdom (496-539)' (reviewer); this dossier cannot start the vassalage before 500.

region.text: Sirmium and its district, Pannonia

ledger.note: 504: Theodoric's forces take Sirmium from the Gepids. 'In 504-505, Theodoric's forces launched a campaign to recover Pannonia and the strategically important town of Sirmium'; the Gepids page has Pitzia expel the Gepid troops from Sirmium in 504 'without much resistance'.

region.text: southern Gaul: Provence with Arles and Marseille

ledger.note: 510: Provence joins the Ostrogothic Kingdom. 'starting in 508, Theodoric's generals campaigned in Gaul' ... 'extending Ostrogothic rule into southern Gaul' 'at the Burgundians' expense'; 'There in 510 Theodoric reestablished the defunct praetorian prefecture of Gaul.' The year is the page's; Cliopatria's 509 Visigothic shape holds the 94 cells (92 of them), so the counterpart is the Visigothic kingdom, as the Visigothic dossier has it; the page's Burgundians are the other candidate. The Battle of Vouille page says only that Theodoric tried to broker peace and that the Visigoths kept Septimania.

region.text: the Visigothic kingdom, from the Atlantic to the Rhone, under Theodoric as regent for Amalaric

ledger.note: 511: Theodoric rules the Visigothic kingdom directly. 'In 511, the Visigothic Kingdom was brought under Theodoric's direct control' after Alaric II fell to Clovis in 507 and Theodoric became regent for his grandson Amalaric (the Ostrogothic Kingdom page: 'ruled as regent of his infant grandson Amalaric').

region.text: the Visigothic kingdom under Amalaric

ledger.note: 526: the Visigothic kingdom is free again. 'After the death of Theodoric on 30 August 526, his achievements began to collapse'; 'the Visigothic kingdom regained its autonomy under Amalaric'. The page dates it to Theodoric's death (526), no month.

region.text: Sicily

ledger.note: December 535: Belisarius takes Sicily. 'Belisarius landed at Sicily, between Byzantine Africa and Italy', and the island was 'quickly taken, with Palermo overcome by late December' 535.

region.text: the southern Alamannian lands, no longer under Ostrogothic protection

ledger.note: 536: the Franks take the Alemanni again. 'The Alemanni were again subjugated by the Franks under Theudebert I in 536' (Alemanni page); the Ostrogothic protection ends.

region.text: Sirmium and its district

ledger.note: 536: Sirmium goes to the Gepids. 'The Gepids had held Sirmium since 536, after taking it from the Byzantine emperor Justinian I' (Cunimund page; the Thurisind page has 537). The pages opened do not say how it passed from the Goths to Justinian; the counterpart is the Eastern Roman Empire, as the Gepid dossier has it (confidence 1: bridging). Sirmium page (read 2026-10-20): 'In 504, Ostrogothic Count Pitzas under Theoderic the Great took Sirmium' and 'After 567, Sirmium was returned to the East Roman Empire'; it is silent on how Sirmium passed to Justinian before the Gepids took it.

region.text: the Alpine edge, Raetia and the south of Alamannia, held through the Alemanni protectorate

ledger.note: 536: the Alpine cells of the old realm go to the Franks. Cliopatria's 533 shape holds 26 cells of Switzerland and Germany (Raetia and the south of Alamannia) that its 536 shape does not and that the Franks' shape holds; the Alemanni page dates the Frankish subjugation of Alamannia to 536. No page opened names Raetia or dates its passing (confidence 1). Theudebert I page (read 2026-10-20): Vitiges 'ceded Provence, part of the Raetia region, and 2,000 pounds of gold' to win Frankish support after he 'assumed power ... in 536'; the page dates the cession to no year, and the Witiges page has Theodahad proposing it, so 536 stays Cliopatria's bridge.

region.text: Dalmatia with Salona

ledger.note: June 536: Dalmatia is lost. 'Mundus took Salona in March but was mortally wounded after a Gothic counterattack. Constantinianus restored Byzantine control of all Dalmatia by late June' 536.

region.text: southern Italy from Rome and Naples to Apulia and Calabria

ledger.note: November-December 536: Naples and Rome. 'Naples was besieged for three weeks and fell in November'; 'Belisarius entered Rome unopposed in December'; the Goths besieged Rome from March 537 to March 538 and failed. The page does not date the submission of Apulia and Calabria. The region is the Eastern Roman Empire dossier's own (Cliopatria's 536 addition).

region.text: the Gothic territory in Gaul, Provence with Arles and Marseille

ledger.note: 540: Gaul passes to the Franks. The Witiges page: 'Theodahad had proposed handing over the Gothic territory in Gaul, along with 2,000 pounds of gold'; the Franks agreed, and Theodahad 'died before the transaction was concluded'. The page gives no year for the handover; Cliopatria's 540 shape no longer holds Provence (125 cells in the Franks' 540 shape), so 540 is the bridge (confidence 1: page silent). Theudebert I page (read 2026-10-20): 'he ceded Provence, part of the Raetia region, and 2,000 pounds of gold' (Vitiges); no year.

region.text: Ravenna, the Emilia and the Po valley, without Verona, Brescia and Pavia

ledger.note: May 540: Ravenna falls. 'In May 540, Belisarius and his army entered Ravenna'; Vitiges was captured. 'The Goths held Ticinum (Pavia), Verona, and parts of the north of the Po.' The region is the Eastern Roman Empire dossier's (Ravenna, the Emilia and the Po valley), less Pavia, which the page leaves to the Goths.
540: the capital moves from Ravenna to Pavia. The infobox gives 'Ravenna (493-540)' then Pavia (540-553).

region.text: Venetia and Liguria

ledger.note: 541: the Goths hold Venetia and Liguria again. 'Gothic control was re-established over Venetia and Liguria under Ildibad' (Goth holdings 541-546); Totila 'was proclaimed king in autumn 541'. The page gives no month for Ildibad's recovery.

region.text: Italy south of the Po and Tuscany, fought over by Totila and the Byzantine armies

ledger.note: Autumn 541: Totila's reconquest begins. 'Gothic resistance was reinvigorated under Totila' in the second phase (541-553); he 'retook much of southern Italy'. The zone is the peninsula south of the Po and Tuscany; the first campaign is dated by the proclamation.

region.text: Naples and its district

ledger.note: 543: Totila takes Naples. 'He retook much of southern Italy, including Naples in 543.'

region.text: Pannonia, south and west of the Danube: the Cliopatria Pannonian shape passing to the Lombards

ledger.note: 546: Pannonia goes to the Lombards. 'The Lombards moved into Pannonia while the Ostrogothic Kingdom was weakened following the death of its founder, Theodoric, in 526'; the Audoin page has the Lombards led to Pannonia 'where they were settled by Justinian I' and the Alboin page's arithmetic puts Audoin on the throne about 547. The page does not date the move; 546 is Cliopatria's year (confidence 1). The Lombard dossier's mirror gain names this dossier; the Audoin page's 'Roman Pannonia' points to the empire instead. Wacho page (read 2026-10-20): reign 'perhaps c. 510' to 539, silent on the Lombards' move to Pannonia; the year stays Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Veneto and Liguria outside Cliopatria's 546 shape and the strongholds: part of Venetia and of Liguria taken by Theudebert I

ledger.note: 546: Venetia and Liguria go in part to the Franks. The Theudebert I page: 'During the Ostrogothic resurgence under King Totila, Theudebert seized the opportunity' and 'captured the Cottian Alps, parts of the Liguria region, and the greater part of Venetia'; he died 'at the end of 547 or the beginning of 548' and Totila reigned from 541. The page dates the capture to no year; 546 is the year Cliopatria's Ostrogothic shape lacks Liguria and half of the Veneto (53 cells drawn here, a lower bound for the 'greater part of Venetia', which is wider than the Veneto region). The Gothic War page has the Goths holding Venetia and Liguria under Ildibad (541) and 'the lands and cities across the River Po' still held by Franks, Alemanni and Goths in 552-555. Confidence 1: the year is a bridge; kingdom-of-the-franks (eu-07) has no matching gain yet.

region.text: Rome and central and southern Italy

ledger.note: 17 December 546: Totila takes Rome. 'Totila ... took Rome on 17 December 546'; the page also says he took it 'in 546 and again in 550'. The region is the Eastern Roman Empire dossier's own, Cliopatria's 546 removal (149 cells: Rome, Campania and the south).

region.text: Rome

ledger.note: Spring 547: Belisarius retakes Rome. 'Belisarius retook Rome in spring 547, but Totila returned later.'

region.text: Rome

ledger.note: 550: Totila takes Rome again. 'Totila took Rome again in 549-550, by suborning part of the garrison to open a gate.' The page spans 549-550; 550 follows the Eastern Roman Empire dossier.

region.text: Rome and the peninsula south of the Po

ledger.note: 552: Narses wins at Taginae and the peninsula is lost. 'The following spring Narses' army met Totila at the Battle of Taginae. Totila was killed in the rout'; 'In October 553, Narses defeated Teias and the last Gothic army in Italy' at Mons Lactarius; Campsa near Naples held out until spring 555. The region is the Eastern Roman Empire dossier's (Rome and the peninsula south of the Po).

region.text: Italy south of the Po and Tuscany

ledger.note: 552: Taginae ends the fight for the peninsula; the last Gothic army falls at Mons Lactarius in October 553 and the Ostrogothic Kingdom page ends the kingdom with Teia's death (552-553).

region.text: Pavia (Ticinum), the capital to 553

ledger.note: 555: Pavia leaves the Gothic shape. The Ostrogothic Kingdom page: infobox 'Pavia (540-553)' and 'With the fall of Ravenna, the capital of the kingdom was brought to Pavia'; the Teia page has Teia withdraw to Ticinum and take the treasury; the Gothic War page makes Verona and Brixia the 'last strongholds' (562), so Pavia fell before. No page (Gothic War, Ostrogothic Kingdom, Teia) dates its fall; 555 is the year of Cliopatria's rump shape, which holds none of Pavia (confidence 1: page silent). The Eastern Roman Empire's dossier holds Pavia from its 540 gain and has no event here.

region.text: Verona and Brescia

ledger.note: 562: the last strongholds fall. 'Verona and Brescia (Brixia) were subjugated in 562'; the Ostrogothic Kingdom page: northern cities 'continued to hold out, however, until the late 560s'.

region.text: the Gothic rump in the north, Verona and Brescia

ledger.note: 562: the Gothic rump ends. The Ostrogothic Kingdom page ends the kingdom with Teia's death (552-553); Cliopatria keeps a Gothic rump in the north to 560 and the Gothic War page has Verona and Brescia, 'the last Gothic and Frankish strongholds', subjugated in 562. This dossier ends the state there.

wars.name: Ostrogothic recovery of Sirmium
wars.outcome: Theodoric's forces recovered Pannonia and Sirmium from the Gepids.
wars.note: The Theodoric the Great page: 'In 504-505, Theodoric extended his realms in the Balkans by defeating the Gepids.' The Gepids page names the comes Pitzia and dates the expulsion from Sirmium 504.

wars.name: Ostrogothic campaign in Gaul
wars.outcome: Theodoric's generals extended Ostrogothic rule into southern Gaul and he reestablished the praetorian prefecture of Gaul in 510.
wars.note: The page says 'at the Burgundians' expense'. The Vouille page: 'Despite Theodoric the Great's attempts to broker a peace between the factions, Clovis began a campaign to seize Aquitaine'; the Visigoths 'retreated to Septimania'. The Provence page opened has nothing on it.

wars.name: Gothic War (535-554)

zones.text: Italy south of the Po and Tuscany

wars.outcome: Justinian's armies reconquered Sicily, Dalmatia and, after Totila's reconquest of 541-552, Italy; the Pragmatic Sanction of 554 settled it and Verona and Brescia fell in 562.
wars.note: The page dates it 535 to 554 in Italy, Dalmatia, Sardinia, Sicily and Corsica. Phases: 535-540 (Belisarius to Ravenna), 541-546 and 547-552 (Totila, Rome 546/547/550), 552-553 (Taginae, Mons Lactarius). Campsa held out to spring 555.

wars.name: Frankish and Alemannic invasions of Italy
wars.outcome: Theudebert I's Franks attacked Goths and Byzantines on the Po in 539 and withdrew with dysentery; 30,000 Franks and Alemanni took Parma in 553 and were destroyed at the Volturnus (554). No border moved.
wars.note: The Ostrogothic Kingdom page: 'Narses also repelled the 554 invasion by the Franks and Alamanni, who were invited by the Goths.'

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is recorded; the Italian coast and the Alps are natural limits, the Danubian and Gallic frontiers are approximate, and the Gothic War front moved year by year.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Ostrogothic Kingdom' 500-560 (seven shapes) is the same realm as the Ostrogoths row 455-499 (eu-06-d: Italy 493-499, rename at 493) and both rows are one state on every page opened; this dossier starts at 500 with the row and ends at 562, two years after the last Cliopatria shape. The orchestrator may merge the two dossiers under 'ostrogoths' (earlier slug) or trim 'ostrogoths' to 492; as written the seam is 499/500 and 'ostrogoths' names this dossier as successor. The 496-499 Alemannic protectorate belongs to 'ostrogoths' and is recorded here at 500. Cliopatria shapes corrected: 500 and 510-535 (Sirmium and Dalmatia; Salona is outside every Ostrogothic shape), 540-545 (the shape is Pannonia with no Italy at all, against the Gothic War page's Pavia, Verona, Brescia, Venetia, Liguria and Totila's south), 546-554 (years). Eastern Roman Empire (eu-05) mirrors: its events 535 Dec, 536 Jun, 536 Dec, 540 May, 543, 546 Dec, 547, 550, 552 and 562 match this ledger in year and region; its 493 vassal_start for the Ostrogothic kingdom is on its side only. Unmirrored: this dossier's 536 loss of Sirmium to the Eastern Roman Empire (it has no Sirmium event before 567), the 541 gain of Venetia and Liguria and the 546 Pannonia loss (its counterpart is the Lombards; the Audoin page says Justinian settled them in 'Roman Pannonia').
